statement: A tile designer draws a convex polygon in which one interior angle measures $120^\circ$ and every other interior angle measures $150^\circ$. How many sides does the polygon have?

choices.misconception: I used $120^\circ$ as the exterior angle at the special vertex instead of $60^\circ$, so $120 + 30(n - 1) = 360$ gave $n = 9$.
I found that there are $10$ angles of $150^\circ$ but forgot to count the $120^\circ$ angle as one more vertex.
I divided $360^\circ$ by the $30^\circ$ exterior angle as if every angle were $150^\circ$, ignoring the one $120^\circ$ angle.

hints: Think about exterior angles. What is the exterior angle at each vertex?
The exterior angles add to $360^\circ$. The special vertex has an exterior angle of $60^\circ$, and each other vertex has an exterior angle of $30^\circ$.

solutions.reliable: The exterior angle at the $120^\circ$ vertex is $60^\circ$, and the exterior angle at each $150^\circ$ vertex is $30^\circ$. The exterior angles of a convex polygon add to $360^\circ$, so $60 + 30(n - 1) = 360$, giving $n - 1 = 10$ and $n = 11$. Check with interior angles: $120 + 10 \cdot 150 = 1620 = 180(11 - 2)$.
solutions.elegant: Using interior angles directly, $120 + 150(n - 1) = 180(n - 2)$ gives $120 + 150n - 150 = 180n - 360$, so $330 = 30n$ and $n = 11$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
